clue.text: Animal returned to Arthur's place?

parts.note: a camel is an animal

indicators.note: returned says the little word to is turned round

explanation.surface: A beast sent back to King Arthur's home.
explanation.definitionFit: Legend places King Arthur's court at a castle of that name; the question mark marks a mythical place.

clue.text: Golfer with clubs first to make mistake

indicators.note: first says the clubs letter comes before the golfer

parts.note: C abbreviates clubs in card games
Bernhard Langer is a German golfer

explanation.surface: A golfer takes his clubs out first and fluffs a shot.
explanation.walkthrough: A CLANGER is British slang for a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a blunder or embarrassing slip, a gaffe.

clue.text: Reddish colour on small leaves on an island

parts.note: maroon is a brownish-red colour
S abbreviates small, as in clothing sizes

explanation.surface: Reddish foliage seen on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like foliage; it is a verb meaning abandons.
explanation.definitionFit: To strand someone on a desert island is to abandon them there; the clue's verb leaves matches this.

clue.text: One finishing school perhaps not a crank

indicators.note: not a says the letter A is dropped from the school leaver

parts.note: a school leaver is one finishing school

explanation.surface: A school leaver who is not an eccentric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crank' looks like an eccentric person; it is a handle, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A crank is a bar or handle turned for mechanical advantage, like a pivoting bar.

clue.text: Call doctor then elope

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters of then elope are altered

explanation.surface: Phone the doctor, then run off to marry.
explanation.definitionFit: To call someone means to ring them on the phone, a verb sense.

clue.text: Whistle-blower concerned with liberal swallowing ecstasy

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: swallowing says the word for liberal takes the drug letter inside it

parts.note: free means liberal, generous
E is the usual abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: An informant who cares about freedom while taking drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: A football official signals with a whistle, so the whistle-blower is the match official, not an informant.

clue.text: Copper dependable? Not at first

indicators.note: not at first says the opening letter is removed from the word for dependable

parts.note: trusty means dependable, reliable

explanation.surface: A doubting question about a reliable policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman; it is the reddish-brown colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Copper-coloured means a reddish-brown shade, like iron oxide corrosion.

clue.text: Your flu is developing in a violent manner

indicators.note: developing means changing form, so the letters of your flu is are rearranged

explanation.surface: A virus getting worse and attacking violently.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting with fury means acting with fierce anger or great force.

clue.text: Wading through town

definitions.meaning: wading through a book is working your way through it page by page
the Berkshire town west of London

explanation.walkthrough: The Berkshire town, west of London, is spelt like the verb form; 'Wading through' is hard going with a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Ploughing through a text is going through it; the town is a large place in Berkshire, England.

clue.text: Dead drunk, texting endlessly about Charlie

indicators.note: about says the shuffled letters go round the Charlie letter
drunk means messed up, so the shortened letters are rearranged
endlessly drops the last letter of texting

parts.note: C is Charlie in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone completely drunk, texting a man named Charlie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' leaves TEXTIN; 'drunk' rearranges it to EXTINT, and 'about' puts it round C.
explanation.definitionFit: A species no longer living has died out, so is dead in that sense.

clue.text: Artist upset by competitor's appearance

indicators.note: upset in a down clue sense of overturned says the artist's letters are turned round

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
a rival is a competitor; the 's links on to the definition

explanation.surface: A painter is unsettled when a rival turns up.
explanation.definitionFit: Making an appearance means turning up, the coming or entry of someone.

clue.text: Man comes from taverns, smashed

indicators.note: smashed means broken up, so the letters of taverns are rearranged

explanation.surface: A drunk man staggers out of the pubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smashed' looks like drunk, describing the man; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Man as a noun can mean a manservant or valet, someone employed to wait on another.

clue.text: Field in which one studies the earth

definitions.text: Field in which one studies the earth

parts.words: Field in which one studies the earth
parts.note: a field of study whose subject is the earth's surface, lands and peoples; field also hints at land

explanation.surface: A description of an academic subject dealing with the planet.
explanation.definitionFit: This school subject describes the physical features of the planet and its regions.

clue.text: Vegetable I put between two legs

indicators.note: put between says the letter I sits in the middle of the two leg words

parts.note: in cricket the leg side is also called on, so two legs give on twice

explanation.surface: Someone holding a vegetable between their legs.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side of the field is also called the on side, so 'leg' gives ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulb eaten as a vegetable, an example of the class.

clue.text: Flowers came up with spades

parts.note: rose is the past tense of rise, came up
S abbreviates spades in card games

explanation.surface: Flowers sprouted when someone dug with spades.
explanation.definitionFit: These are an example of garden blooms, the classic red flower.

clue.text: Nick spells strings of words?

definitions.meaning: nick is British slang for prison, and spells there are terms of imprisonment
a grammatical unit of words in a row

explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' is British slang for prison, so 'Nick spells' are prison terms; 'spells' tempts towards spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Prison terms are handed down by a judge; a grammatical unit is a string of words.

clue.text: Groan, consumed by obvious lapse

indicators.note: consumed by says the groan word is swallowed inside the word for obvious

parts.note: overt means open, obvious
a sigh is a groan of weariness

explanation.surface: Someone moans at an obvious slip.
explanation.definitionFit: A careless lapse is a failure to notice, an unintentional mistake.

clue.text: German city starts to treat immigrants as legally required

parts.note: Essen is a city in the Ruhr, Germany

indicators.note: starts to picks the first letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A German city deciding how to treat new arrivals under the law.
explanation.definitionFit: Something indispensable is absolutely necessary, required.

clue.text: Plots in Greene's novel

indicators.note: novel means new, fresh, so the letters of in Greene's are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Talk of the storylines in a Graham Greene book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' pretends to be a book by Greene; it is the anagram signal, and 'Plots' is a verb, not storylines.
explanation.definitionFit: To plot is to contrive or scheme, so these verbs both mean arranges craftily.

clue.text: Impassioned former lover advanced

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
cited means put forward, advanced as an argument

explanation.surface: An ex-partner making a heated case.
explanation.definitionFit: Stirred up, aroused, worked up with strong feeling.

clue.text: Excellent run produces cheers

parts.note: good means excellent
a bye is a run scored in cricket without the batsman hitting the ball

explanation.surface: A great run of play gets the crowd cheering.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a bye is a run taken when the ball passes the batsman untouched. 'cheers' is British informal for farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheers is informal British for farewell, a word said when leaving.

clue.text: Back in saddle I yearn to climb down

indicators.note: Back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A rider in the saddle wanting to get off the horse.
explanation.definitionFit: To climb down is to back down or give way in an argument, to concede.

clue.text: Joy, maybe, from Beethoven's second movement

indicators.note: second picks the second letter of the composer name before it

parts.note: motion means movement

explanation.surface: The happy second movement of a Beethoven symphony.
explanation.definitionFit: Joy is an example of a feeling, hence the maybe.

clue.text: Wise men after party getting quantities of medicine

indicators.note: after says the wise men come behind the party

parts.note: a do is a party
sages are wise men

explanation.surface: Wise men at a party taking their medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: A measured amount of a drug to be taken is a dose, the given quantity.

clue.text: Finish third in race and be defeated

indicators.note: third in picks the third letter of the word race

parts.note: to lose is to be defeated

explanation.surface: A runner comes third and loses the race.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring something to a close is to end it, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Bribe American with cheap second homes

parts.note: a bung is British slang for a bribe
low means cheap, as in low prices

explanation.surface: Buying cheap holiday houses with a sweetener paid to an American.
explanation.walkthrough: BUNG is everyday British slang for a bribe or backhander.
explanation.definitionFit: These are an example of houses, single-storey dwellings.

clue.text: Wide thoroughfare south of Belgium

indicators.note: south of in a down clue puts the road below the Belgium letter

parts.note: B is the international vehicle code for Belgium
a road is a thoroughfare

explanation.surface: A wide street in the south of Belgium.
explanation.definitionFit: Wide and expansive mean of great width, a plain synonym.

clue.text: By the side of a pine

parts.note: to pine for something is to long for it

explanation.surface: Standing next to a pine tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pine' looks like the tree; it is the verb to yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: Running beside something, as a path lies beside a river, is a preposition sense.

clue.text: Preparing cocoa but heartlessly leaves

indicators.note: preparing means making up, so the letters are mixed into a new form
heartlessly drops the middle of but, keeping its outside letters

explanation.surface: Someone making hot chocolate and leaving coldly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartlessly' leaves BT from BUT; with COCOA these letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The plant is grown and dried for its leaves, which are smoked.

clue.text: Strength in golf decreasing?

parts.note: iron stands for strength, as in an iron will
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A golfer whose power is fading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decreasing' looks like getting smaller; split it as de-creasing. 'golf' also tempts towards the iron club.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as de-creasing, the word means removing creases, which is pressing clothes flat.

clue.text: Regularly tenses head after doctor put a bandage on

indicators.note: after says the editor letters for head follow the doctor and the regular letters
regularly takes every other letter of tenses

parts.note: ED, an editor, is the head of a newspaper

explanation.surface: A doctor's assistant stiffly bandages a patient's head.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressing a wound means covering it with a bandage or sterile pad.

clue.text: Celebrities, for example, restricted by loans

indicators.note: restricted by says the example abbreviation is held inside the word for loans

parts.note: lends means loans, gives on loan

explanation.surface: Famous people being held back by debts.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone famous in their field is called a living great, a star.
